2608.11922.title: LODESTAR: Trustworthy Entropy Is Navigated, Not Merely Measured -- Reinforced Polarizer Keeps a Frozen LLM from Being Confidently Misled by the Wrong Evidence
2608.11922.paper_summary: Predictive-distribution entropy makes a strong selection rule in retrieval-augmented question answering: across five QA benchmarks, keeping the candidate answer that a frozen respondent LLM produces with the lowest answer-token entropy lifts mean answer $F_1$ from 0.4769 to 0.5148 over the retriever's top-ranked passage, with no gold answers. Yet this lowest-entropy rule, which prior entropy-based selectors adopt, fails in a specific and consequential way: a misleading passage makes the respondent confidently wrong, driving its entropy down precisely where the signal looks most trustworthy. We show that the failure comes from the passage the respondent reads -- and the context that passage is read in is an input we can intervene on. We introduce LODESTAR, to our knowledge the first method to score a text intervention by the uncertainty it induces in a third-party frozen respondent, compared across one question's candidates. LODESTAR uses reinforcement learning to train, once and offline, a polarizer -- a short fixed natural-language string inserted into the respondent's prompt and never into its weights; its training labels are built offline from gold answers and two LLM judges, and inference reads neither. Evaluating every competing selector under the same frozen respondent and the same candidate pools on 5,008 questions, LODESTAR attains the highest mean $F_1$ of any inference-ready selector (0.5148 to 0.5339), the highest exact match (0.4136), and the highest GPT-4o judge score of the frozen-respondent configurations judged (0.6435); its three-seed mean wins all 70 method-by-dataset $F_1$ cells against fourteen published configurations while remaining paired-significant against every one. The gain holds both in-domain and out-of-domain, and ablating the polarizer shows it is what makes the respondent read a misleading passage less often (26.0% against 30.3%).
2608.11922.paper_summary_zh: 預測分佈熵在檢索增強問答中形成了一個強有力的選擇規則：在五個QA基準中，保持一個冷凍的回應者LLM產生的最低回答標記熵的候選答案，將平均回答$F_1$從0.4769提升至0.5148，儘管沒有金標答案。然而，這一最低熵規則，先前基於熵的選擇器所採用，卻以一種特定且重大的方式失敗：一個誤導性的段落使得回應者自信地錯誤，驅動其熵在信號看起來最可信的地方下降。我們表明，失敗來自回應者所閱讀的段落——而該段落被閱讀的上下文是我們可以介入的輸入。我們介紹了LODESTAR，據我們所知，這是第一種通過它在第三方冷凍回應者中引起的不確定性來評分文本干預的方法，並在一個問題的候選者中進行比較。LODESTAR使用強化學習進行訓練，一次性和離線地，生成一個極化器——一個短的固定自然語言字符串，插入到回應者的提示中，並且從不進入其權重；其訓練標籤是從金標答案和兩位LLM評審離線構建的，推理時不讀取這些。對5,008個問題下的每個競爭選擇器進行評估，使用相同的冷凍回應者和相同的候選池，LODESTAR達到了任何推理準備選擇器中最高的平均$F_1$（從0.5148提升至0.5339）、最高的精確匹配（0.4136）以及被評審的冷凍回應者配置中最高的GPT-4o評審分數（0.6435）；其三種種子的平均在與十四個已發表配置的70個方法-數據集$F_1$單元中獲勝，同時對每一個保持配對顯著性。這一增益在域內和域外均成立，而去除極化器顯示它是使回應者較少閱讀誤導性段落的原因（26.0%對30.3%）。
